title.value: QRelScore: Better Evaluating Generated Questions with Deeper Understanding of Context-aware Relevance
title.justification: This is the title mentioned at the beginning and throughout the document, focusing on evaluating generated questions by understanding context-aware relevance.
title.quote: QRelScore: Better Evaluating Generated Questions with Deeper Understanding of Context-aware Relevance

extractions.description: The paper presents QRelScore, a new evaluation metric for the automatic assessment of question generation systems which emphasizes the context-aware relevance of the generated questions. It leverages pre-trained language models to achieve better alignment with human judgments and robustness to adversarial examples compared to existing metrics.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on evaluating generated questions in natural language processing, emphasizing deeper context understanding rather than directly relating to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Existing metrics for assessing question generation not only require costly human reference but also fail to take into account the input context of generation, rendering the lack of deep understanding of the relevance between the generated questions and input contexts.

primary_category.justification: The research is centered around computational linguistics and natural language processing improvements, not directly tied to any climate or sustainability-focused category.
primary_category.quote: QRelScore addresses the weaknesses above by considering the context-aware relevance in a word- and sentence-level manner.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not tackle multiple areas within Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as its themes remain solely within improving question generation evaluation models.
secondary_categories.quote: Compared with existing metrics, our experiments demonstrate that QRelScore is able to achieve a higher correlation with human judgments while being much more robust to adversarial samples.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category applicable as the content does not engage with sustainability or ecological matters.
primary_sub_category.quote: QRelScore presents an automatic reference-free evaluation metric for question generation (QG), requiring neither supervision from human ratings nor additional training on specific domains.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Because the main focus is on question generation metrics, it does not cross into ecological or climate sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Results reveal that previous metrics such as BERTScore can correctly assign lower scores to the candidates of low quality, but it performs poorly in the candidates of high quality.

applications.justification: The specific application of this research lies in enhancing the accuracy and reliability of automatic evaluations for question generation within NLP.
applications.quote: Question generation (QG) systems aim to generate natural language questions that are relevant to and usually can be answered by a given piece of input text.

new_primary_category.justification: While the proposed metrics offer improvements in evaluating language models, they do not define or introduce a new sustainability category.
new_primary_category.quote: Traditional automatic metrics (e.g. BLEU, ROUGE...) measure the n-gram overlap between the candidate and corresponding reference question, but they often fail to robustly match paraphrases.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no indication in the paper that it extends into or necessitates the creation of a new sub-category related to sustainability.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: As an important natural language generation task, QG can be used to improve various applications, such as question answering (QA)...
